title: National Consumer Credit Protection (Fees) Amendment (Registries Modernisation) Bill 2019
short_title: National Consumer Credit Protection (Fees) Amendment (Registries Modernisation) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would modernise Commonwealth business registers and introduce a director identification number (DIN) requirement.
The package would allow a minister to appoint an existing Commonwealth body as registrar, with functions and powers set out in existing laws like the Corporations Act and the Credit Act.

A person appointed as a director under the Corporations Act or the CATSI Act would have to apply for a DIN before their appointment, with a 28-day grace period during the first year of the requirement.
changes: The bill would modernise Commonwealth business registers, initially covering those administered by ASIC and the Australian Business Register.
The bill would introduce a DIN requirement for directors of bodies corporate under the Corporations Act and the CATSI Act.
The bill would create civil and criminal penalties for directors who fail to apply for a DIN on time or who provide false information.
summary.affected: Directors of bodies corporate registered under the Corporations Act and the CATSI Act, and officials handling information held by the registrar.
